Subject: Request: topology and evidence for PrivEdge (SOC 2 review)

Hi Rafael,

We're starting the SOC 2 scoping for Veridian and need a concise architecture package that explains how PrivEdge (your private deployment option) enforces tenant isolation and protects customer keys and telemetry. Specifically we need:

- A one-page network topology showing control-plane vs data-plane separation and egress controls (redacted CIDRs are fine).
- A short narrative on how KMS boundaries are enforced and whether HSM-backed keys are supported.
- Evidence of audit/log retention and where traces are stored for Private deployments.
- Any existing SIG/CAIQ mappings you have that reference these controls.

Can you get something to me by COB next Tue? If there's a prebuilt packet you can attach, that would work.

Thanks,
Elena Ross
Sr. InfoSec Manager, Veridian Systems
security@veridian.com

Original: Dan Sullivan (cc'd) asked that we include any escalation contacts and a short runbook for emergency key rotation.
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 7 May 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: topology and evidence for PrivEdge (SOC 2 review)

Elena,

Thanks — we can absolutely assemble that. Attaching a concise topology (privedge-topology-v1.pdf) that highlights: control-plane isolation, data-plane enclaves, egress proxying, and our KMS boundary model. A few notes up front:

- Control plane: runs in a customer-dedicated control namespace inside the customer's VPC for Private deployments, or in a logically separated control tenancy for Dedicated contracts. We include mutual TLS and per-route RBAC.
- Data plane: model-level inference runs in isolated GPU pools (tenant-scoped runtime pods/enclaves). KV caches are ephemeral and tenant-scoped.
- Egress controls: default deny with explicit egress proxies; customers can approve outbound IP ranges or route through their own NAT.
- KMS: supports cloud KMS integrations and customer-managed keys (CMK); HSM-backed keys supported when requested via our Dedicated/Private onboarding.

I've attached an initial diagram and a short manifest listing artifacts we can provide for SOC 2 / SIG review. Ben, could you add the retention sample and the annotated controlplane flow?

Next steps:
1) I'll schedule a 30-min walkthrough early next week to talk through the diagram and answer questions.
2) We'll produce a redaction-friendly PDF set and a CSV checklist mapping of SIG/CAIQ controls.

Rafael Mendes
Principal Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference

Elena / Dan,

Following up with the packet we discussed. Attached artifacts (redacted where appropriate) and a short summary below. Live walkthrough: I've scheduled a 30-minute session for Tue 10 May 2027 at 10:00 PT (calendar invite to follow).

Package contents (all files attached or in the shared Drive link):
- privedge-topology-v1.pdf (one-page redacted network topology, shows control-plane vs data-plane and egress proxies)
- controlplane-flow-annotated.pdf (sequence of control-plane calls, mutual TLS & RBAC annotations)
- segmentation-ribbon-drilldown.png (internal explainer — redaction-allowed)
- kms-boundary-checklist.xlsx (maps supported KMS modes: Redwood-managed, customer-managed, HSM-backed)
- audit-retention-sample.log (snipped example that demonstrates tenant_id tagging and retention metadata)
- evidence-manifest-VER-20270507.txt (human-readable manifest with file checksums and short descriptions)

Short summary:
- Isolation model: tenants run in isolated runtime enclaves on dedicated GPU pools; control-plane endpoints are authenticated and scoped per-customer. We employ automatic KV cache eviction and network egress proxies to limit lateral movement.
- KMS: we support cloud KMS integrations (GCP/AWS/Azure) and can bring-your-own-key; for customers requiring HSM-backed keys, we deploy Customer KMS connectors in the control-plane namespace and perform periodic rotation via our ops runbook.
- Logging & retention: audit events are emitted with tenant_id and request_id tags and stored in a customer-scoped bucket for Private deployments; retention policy configurable at onboarding (examples included).
- SIG/CAIQ mapping: included in the Drive link is a working CSV that maps our architecture components to common questionnaire controls (this is a living artifact).

If you need a condensed one-page narrative (for your security packet) I can provide that by Monday. Please use the Drive link for downloads: https://drive.redwood.internal/privedge/VER-20270507/topology (access granted to your security group).

Thanks,
Rafael Mendes
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
